transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-11
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (EntTech Head of IT), Michael O'Connor (EntTech Sec Eng), Priya Desai (EntTech Platform Lead)

Summary: quick security & compliance review focused on SSO (SAML), SCIM provisioning, and RBAC/least-privilege model. Discussed SAML cert rotation, SCIM group sync, audit logs retention and KMS/encryption at rest, plus multi-tenant role mapping and emergency access patterns.

Topics: SSO/SAML setup, SCIM provisioning, RBAC roles, audit logging & retention, KMS/encryption, SOC 2 considerations, data residency

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, we'll keep this focused on SSO, SCIM and RBAC mapping today; Daniel will cover the heavy config bits.
[00:22] Daniel Cho: Hi all, yeah, hi. Quick agenda, 1) SAML flow and metadata, 2) SCIM attributes and group provisioning, 3) RBAC patterns and least-privilege, 4) audit logs and encryption, and then next steps.
[00:35] Laura Kim: Sounds good. We're evaluating multiple vendors and want to make sure provisioning fits our team structure, also cert rotation policy and who has admin, etc.
[00:42] Michael O'Connor: Yeah and we have strict requirements on audit trails and KMS integration — we use AWS KMS and have a HSM for keys, we need to understand how Redwood integrates.
[01:00] Daniel Cho: Great. For SAML we support IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows, standard SAML 2.0. You can upload your IdP metadata or we can provide ours. Typical attributes we look for are email, firstName, lastName and group membership (we accept memberOf or custom attribute).
[01:20] Priya Desai: For group mapping: we have groups for eng-prod, eng-staging, analyst, security, and a couple of cross-functional groups. How granular should we get?
[01:32] Daniel Cho: Good question. For RBAC we recommend mapping groups to roles in Redwood: Admin, Platform-Engineer (able to deploy), Viewer, Billing (if you want cost visibility), and a Support role with read-only logs. Keep it least-privilege — don't map org-admin to Redwood Admin unless they truly need it.
[01:50] Maya Patel: One thing customers ask is about dynamic provisioning via SCIM — we support SCIM 2.0. You can provision users and groups from your IdP, and we will sync adds/removes and group membership changes.
[02:08] Laura Kim: Is there a delay on deprovisioning? We need immediate removal for terminated users.
[02:14] Daniel Cho: SCIM sync is near real-time; typical propagation is under a minute for single user changes, but bulk changes can take longer — we also provide a manual deprovision API for emergency revoke.
[02:30] Michael O'Connor: Good, and do you enforce SAML certificate rotation? How frequently? We have a 90-day rotation policy.
[02:38] Daniel Cho: We support certificate rollover patterns — you can upload the new cert and mark it active; we recommend coordinating a short overlap window to avoid downtime. We also have automation guides for cert rotation in our docs. We'll share the guide link after the call.
[02:55] Priya Desai: For SCIM group mapping, do you support nested groups or only flat groups?
[03:01] Daniel Cho: Currently we handle flat group membership; nested groups can be flattened on the IdP side or we can accept a custom attribute that resolves membership. There are a few customers where that was needed and we provided a small mapping layer.
[03:18] Laura Kim: About RBAC — can roles be scoped to projects or just org/application wide?
[03:24] Daniel Cho: Roles today are per-organization with resource-level permissions; you can create per-project permission sets via our Console and assign groups to those roles. For most customers we recommend a 3-tier role model: Org Admin (very few), Project Admins, and Viewer/Analyst roles.
[03:40] Michael O'Connor: Audit logs — retention and export. We need immutable logs for 1 year, ideally sent to our SIEM (Splunk).
[03:48] Maya Patel: Redwood has audit log export; you can stream logs to an S3 bucket or push to syslog/Splunk via Fluentd. Retention is configurable; for enterprise we support long-term retention and exports for compliance.
[04:05] Daniel Cho: Note on immutability — logs are write-once in our system; for additional control you can stream to a customer-managed S3 with object lock if you need WORM storage.
[04:18] Priya Desai: Encryption at rest and KMS integration — we use customer-managed keys in AWS KMS. Can Redwood use our keys?
[04:26] Daniel Cho: Yes, for Private deployments we support BYOK with integrations to AWS KMS and HSMs. For Hosted, we offer a customer-managed KMS option where you give a key policy and we wrap data keys. We'll need to share the KMS integration checklist.
[04:41] Laura Kim: Data residency — some of our data must stay in EU. Can you pin customer data and logs to region?
[04:48] Maya Patel: We support region pinning for enterprise plans — you can choose EU, US, or APAC regions, and logs can be kept in-region. For Private/on-prem we obviously keep everything customer-side.
[05:00] Michael O'Connor: SOC 2 — do you have reports and a subprocessor list?
[05:05] Maya Patel: Yes, we are SOC 2 Type II and have an annual audit; we can share the SOC 2 report and a standard subprocessor list under NDA.
[05:12] Priya Desai: For RBAC least-privilege, any recommendations for emergency access? We use break-glass accounts with MFA.
[05:19] Daniel Cho: Break-glass is supported — you can create a timed elevated access role with approval workflow, and all actions are logged and require justification. We recommend using short TTLs and requiring MFA plus a ticket ID.
[05:33] Laura Kim: For attribute mapping, we have email aliases and separate login emails, how tolerant is Redwood with the NameID?
[05:39] Daniel Cho: We can accept email as NameID or a persistent unique id; if you have aliases, it's better to use a unique external id and send primary email as an attribute. We have mapping rules in the Console.
[05:54] Maya Patel: A couple of practical items — we'll send the SAML metadata and SCIM endpoint details, the cert-rotation doc, and an RBAC mapping template so you can drop your groups in.
[06:05] Michael O'Connor: On audit logs streaming, what about sensitive fields in logs — do you mask PII?
[06:12] Daniel Cho: By default we redact obvious PII fields and support configurable scrubbing rules; you can choose to mask or fully redact sensitive attributes before they leave Redwood.
[06:24] Priya Desai: Any limitations with SCIM around group size or rate limits?
[06:29] Daniel Cho: We have rate limits on SCIM for bulk operations (we'll include those in the guide). Groups up to tens of thousands are supported but massive bulk imports should be batched.
[06:42] Laura Kim: One more on compliance — do you support SCIM/SSO for service accounts? We have CI/CD bots that need scoped access.
[06:49] Daniel Cho: We recommend using service principals rather than user-mapped accounts; service principals can be given scoped API keys with restricted scopes and short TTLs, plus they can be tied to IP allow lists.
[07:05] Maya Patel: Ok let's recap next steps — Maya to send docs, Laura to share metadata/attributes, Daniel to draft RBAC mapping. Schedule follow-up deep-dive with engineering.
[07:18] Laura Kim: Works for me. Thanks all.
[07:22] Michael O'Connor: Thanks.
[07:25] End meeting.
